Key state-machine decisions (all documented in `README.md`):

- `record_ended` makes a terminator **end** a record instead of starting an empty one (`a\n` → 1 record; `"\n"` → `[[""]]`; `""` → 0 records).
- `field_pending` makes a trailing comma open one more empty field (`a,` → `["a",""]`, `,,,` → 4 fields).
- `CR`, `LF`, `CRLF` are all record terminators (CRLF as one); inside quotes they are literal content, preserved verbatim.
- Rejects unterminated quotes, `"` in unquoted fields, any non-separator text after a closing quote (including whitespace and `\"`-style escapes), and ragged records. Field values are never trimmed; everything is a string.

- Fields split on `,`; empty fields are `""`; no trimming.

## HPACK codec implemented (RFC 7541) — `moon test`: 92/92 pass, `moon check`: 0 errors

### Implementation (root `hpack` package, split by functional area)

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `integer.mbt` | Prefixed integers (§5.1): N-bit prefix + base-128 continuation octets, minimal encoding, `IntegerOverflow` for values above 2³¹−1 and for >5 continuation octets (permitted by §5.1). The overflow test is applied to the *headroom* before the addition, so neither the shift nor the sum can wrap. |
| `huffman.mbt` | §5.2 string-literal codec: MSB-first packing with EOS-bit padding; decoding walks a flat binary trie over the Appendix B code, rejecting EOS in data, padding >7 bits, and padding that is not all ones. |
| `huffman_table.mbt`, `static_table.mbt` | Appendix B code lengths/codes plus the derived decoding automaton, and Appendix A's 61 entries — **transcribed from `specs/rfc7541.txt` by a generator that also verified the code is complete and prefix-free**, so nothing is hand-typed. |
| `dynamic_table.mbt` | §§4.1–4.4: exact `name+value+32` accounting, newest-first indices, eviction on insert/size change, "entry larger than the table empties it and is not inserted", name resolved before the eviction that removes it, saturating size arithmetic. |
| `decoder.mbt` | All five representations of §6 over one connection-wide table; index 0 / past-the-end → `InvalidIndex`, size updates only before the first field and never above the decoder's limit, truncated integers/strings → `UnexpectedEof`. |
| `encoder.mbt` | The deterministic greedy strategy (exact → smallest index; name match → smallest name index with incremental indexing + insert; else literal name), `use_huffman` Huffman-coding *every* literal, both non-indexing single-field forms (never insert, never emit size updates), and §4.2 signalling (smallest requested size first, then final size). |

## INI parser implemented (MoonBit) — `moon test`: 92/92 pass, `moon check`: 0 errors

### What I built
A real line-oriented parser for the repo's INI dialect, in the root `ini` package, split by responsibility:

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `ini_error.mbt` | `pub suberror IniParseError { Malformed(line~, message~) }` + `Show` |
| `text.mbt` | blank/comment/separator/control char classes, `split_lines` (LF/CRLF), trailing-backslash counting, `EscapeStyle` + `decode_escapes` |
| `value.mbt` | quoted-value scanning (same-line closing, escaped-quote rules, trailing-junk check), inline-comment stripping, continuation gathering |
| `entry.mbt` | first `=`/`:` wins, key trim/validation, carrier selection |
| `section.mbt` | `[name]` scanning, nested-bracket/empty/trailing-text rejection, wrapping-quote removal |
| `parser.mbt` | `pub fn parse(StringView) -> Doc raise`: line classification, global section vs. section maps, reopen/last-wins |
| `printer.mbt` | `pub fn print(Doc) -> String`: every value double-quoted with `\\ \" \n \r \t` escaping; section names quoted only when needed |
| `ini_edge_test.mbt` | 80 authored edge-case tests (all spec items + round-trip and 2000-iteration property runs) |
| `README.md` | architecture, pipeline, escape tables, continuation table, error list, design decisions, testing guide |

Key semantics: continuation decided on the raw line before escapes (odd run = marker, even = literals); a continuation line contributes text only (its `=`, `:`, quotes and comment markers are ordinary, so inline comments are stripped only on the entry's own line); each carrier decodes only its own escapes; a trailing newline terminates the last line, so a dangling marker errors; values are trimmed/stripped only when unquoted.

A genuine, line-oriented INI parser for this repo's dialect, in MoonBit, split by pipeline stage:

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `scanner.mbt` (150) | Line splitting (LF/CRLF; trailing terminator adds no line), blank/trim helpers, trailing-backslash run counter, control-char detection |

| `parse_error.mbt` (17) | `ParseError { Malformed(line, message) }` |

Key algorithm decisions, each derived from `specs/ini.md` rather than fixtures:

* **Raw text first, escapes second.** Continuation is decided on the raw physical line by the *parity* of the trailing backslash run, inline-comment cutting and trimming also run before decoding, so `k=a\\` (escaped literal) and `k=a\` (marker) stay distinguishable; the whole N=1..4 run-length table is reproduced.
* **Continuation lines contribute text, not syntax** (their `=`, `:`, quotes, `;`/`#` are literal), and a marker with no following line raises.
* **Separator = first `=` or `:`**; keys verbatim after trimming, rejected when empty/blank/control-bearing.
* **Quoted values** close on the same line, only blanks/an optional comment may follow, keep inner blanks and comment markers, and decode only their own escape set (`\"` only in `"…"`, `\'` only in `'…'`, `\n\r\t` not in `'…'`).
* **Inline comments** require a preceding blank; **sections** trim, strip one wrapping quote pair, reject nesting/empty/blank names and trailing junk.
